title: fidelity-concierge-thinking-log
content:
Context / one-liner:
An inline ‘Fidelity Concierge’ that watches an active assistant session and proactively suggests lower-cost, condensed, or structured alternatives for specific turns or session segments. The concierge gives a lightweight preview and a quick toggle so end-users (or client apps) can accept a cheaper/shorter response without breaking flow.

Why bother (problem):
- Many teams want to lower per-session token spend but don’t want blunt global economy modes.
- Current fallback lanes either require dev configuration (A/B rollout) or are too coarse (full-economy mode).
- Users sometimes want a one-off shorter/summary answer, or a structured payload, without changing agent persona or session fidelity permanently.

Hypothesis:
- Exposing contextual micro-fidelity choices will reduce average tokens per session by ~15–30% for eligible queries while keeping user satisfaction >= 90% of baseline.
- Developer adoption will be driven by minimal integration effort (single opt-in flag + response hooks).

Non-goals:
- Not replacing model-level rollouts or dedicated autoscaling policies.
- Not a full user-facing settings page to manage permanent fidelity defaults (that’s a follow-up).

Core concepts / UX flow (sketch):
1) Detection: runtime flags + lightweight heuristic to mark a turn as "concierge-candidate" (long generation, retrieval-heavy, or repeat clarification).
2) Proposal: a short alternate response is synthesized (summary / bullet / structured JSON / low-token variant). Show a 1–2 line preview in the client.
3) Acceptance: user taps "Use short" or an app auto-accepts based on policy. Then full answer may still be available via "Show full".
4) Telemetry: annotate which turns used concierge, final tokens, satisfaction events.

Edge variants to support: 
- Summarize: compress long assistant turn to N tokens (configurable: 30/75/200).
- Structured: convert to JSON schema (for tool consumers).
- Guided Qs: generate a short follow-up question instead of a full answer to gather missing info.
- Rollback: allow expanding to full answer on demand.

User stories (rough):
- As an end-user, I want a "Short answer" button so I can get a quick result when I'm in a hurry.
- As a product admin, I want to opt-in to Concierge mode for certain routes so my customers see cheaper variants.
- As an integration engineer, I want an API flag and a response hook so I can decide server-side whether to accept the concierge output.

Acceptance criteria (minimal MVP):
- API: requests can include concierge=true and optional max_tokens_hint.
- Runtime: server returns primary_response + concierge_alternative (preview text + token_estimate) when candidate heuristics fire.
- Client: sample web client shows preview + Accept/Expand controls.
- Metrics: record tokens_saved, concierge_accept_rate, and NPS-proxy event.

Success metrics (first 8 weeks):
- adoption: concierge flag used on >= 5% of hosted sessions for participating customers.
- econ: mean tokens/session decreases by >=12% for sessions with concierge accepted.
- quality: concierge-accepted sessions have satisfaction >= 0.9 * baseline (survey or proxy).

Data / telemetry we need:
- per-turn: candidate_reason, primary_tokens, concierge_tokens, accepted(bool), user_expand(bool), timestamp.
- per-session: cumulative_tokens_saved, acceptance_rate, churn signals.

Experiment plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (dev sandbox): local runtime + toy client, heuristic toggle.
- Phase 1 (internal beta): 2 internal teams + console feature flag; collect telemetry, manual QA.
- Phase 2 (opt-in customers): 3 customers across different verticals; measure econ and quality.
- Phase 3 (broad opt-in): UI polish, SDK helpers, default heuristics.

Technical considerations / runtime work: 
- Heuristic engine: small scoring function that runs pre-generation and decides whether to synthesize alt. Must be <2ms additional latency on fast paths.
- Synthesis: alternative response can be produced by a smaller/cheaper model variant or the same model with constrained generation params. Evaluate both.
- KV/cache/tokens: if using smaller model, reuse retrieval outputs & context to avoid re-RAG cost.
- Telemetry: new schema (lightweight) and tagging. Backfill to console.

Console + API delta:
- New API param: concierge: {enabled:true, max_tokens_hint: 75, mode: "summary|structured|followup"}.
- Console: per-route toggle + acceptance/usage dashboard.

Dependencies / blockers: 
- small-model lineup: need validated <7B variants that produce acceptable condensations.
- console schema work: route-level flags + new telemetry panels.
- SDK helpers: simple helpers for web + mobile to surface preview UI.

Risks / mitigations: 
- Risk: concierge generates incorrect/unsafe terse answers. 
  Mitigation: require safety checks + explicit accept before committing use in downstream systems; surface provenance.
- Risk: users confuse "short" with authoritative answer.
  Mitigation: UI microcopy, trust badges, and easy expand.

Open questions / TODOs (brain-dump):
- Heuristic rules: should they be ML-based (classifier) or deterministic thresholds? Quick start: deterministic with telemetry for classifier training.
- Who pays for the alt synthesis? Should acceptance trigger billing for full tokens or discounted tokens? Need billing policy.
- Metrics: define exact experiment proxies (survey event vs implicit expand).
- Integration: if a third-party consumer accepts concierge alt programmatically, what guarantees do we provide? 

Next immediate steps (short list):
- Prototype: wire up concierge flag + small-model alt in local runtime (2 engineer-days).
- Mock client: create minimal web demo with preview/accept/expand (1 PM + 1 FE day).
- Telemetry: add proto schema to console backlog (CONFLUENCE:incubator/fidelity-concierge).
- Sync: quick sync with Mika and Noam to align on safety and small-model candidates.

Notes to self:
- Keep design minimal for MVP: preview + accept + expand. Don’t over-index on admin UI at first.
- Strongly prefer reusing existing batching/caching infra to avoid redoing retrieval.
- Consider a "session-level budget" policy that auto-accepts concierge once a token budget threshold is hit.

Random thought: add a developer toggle to show "estimated cost saved" in the preview (for pro accounts) — good marketing/observability hook.

End of page.
